payload.name: truewire 0.1.0
payload.body:
Published to [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/truewire/0.1.0/) as `truewire==0.1.0`.

First release of the toolchain: `truewire init | import openapi | check | examples | surface | generate python | mock | mcp | standards | docs`. A directory-per-endpoint spec format with an 18-rule linter, recorded-example coverage with honest `unverified` reasons, an HTTP and WebSocket mock server that replays recorded examples, a Python generator with runtime validation and pagination walkers, an OpenAPI 3.0/3.1 importer, and an MCP server that exposes a project's endpoints as tools. `init` writes a `pyproject.toml` so the generated client installs with `pip install -e .`.

Verified before this PR: 887 toolchain tests green, ruff clean, wheel built with `uv build`, installed into a clean Python 3.12 venv and exercised through the README quickstart end to end (init, import, check, generate, `pip install -e .`, mock server, typed call returning a real `datetime`).

Merging this PR publishes `truewire==0.1.0` to PyPI through Trusted Publishing, pushes the `truewire-v0.1.0` tag and creates the GitHub release (`release-truewire.yml`). Merge the `truewire-core` release PR first: this package depends on `truewire-core>=0.1.0`, so `pip install truewire` only resolves once the runtime is on PyPI.

payload.name: truewire-core 0.1.0
payload.body:
Published to [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/truewire-core/0.1.0/) as `truewire-core==0.1.0`.

First release of the runtime behind clients generated by `truewire`: HTTP and WebSocket transports, runtime validation, pagination walkers, timestamp converters and typed error types. Forked from `typed-core` and renamed; `EpochConverter` now uses integer arithmetic so nanosecond timestamps round-trip exactly.

Verified before this PR: 83 runtime tests green, wheel built with `uv build`, installed into a clean Python 3.12 venv together with `truewire` and exercised through the README quickstart (init, import, check, generate, `pip install -e .`, mock server, typed call).

Merging this PR publishes `truewire-core==0.1.0` to PyPI through Trusted Publishing, pushes the `truewire-core-v0.1.0` tag and creates the GitHub release (`release-core.yml`). Merge this one before the `truewire` release PR: `truewire` depends on `truewire-core>=0.1.0`.
